correctness.rationale: All ideals uniquely correspond to projected subspace S, central intersection T containing [S,V], and a linear graph lift S→Z/T. In the star case S not within U forces T=Z, while S within U has image dimension dim S. The two exhaustive cases produce the polynomial. The leading powers of q in the Gaussian coefficients prove the n>=4 large-field distribution. Exhaustive direct-bracket checks cover (n,q)=(1,2),(1,3),(1,5),(2,2),(2,3),(3,2), independently of the classification.

Integral ideal-zeta and finite-group subgroup enumerations are a residual priority risk, not an asserted exhaustive negative.

value.rationale: The ideal-dimension polynomial is a natural complete structural invariant for the entire distinctly labeled star Lie family and all finite fields; ideals govern quotient algebras and adjoint-invariant subspaces. The nontrivial graph-lift contribution is essential and the polynomial yields a parity-sensitive large-field typical-dimension law. The result is not a small finite table or a restatement of abelian-factor/rigidity calculations.
